question: Which international body sets the essential competencies required for basic midwifery education and practice?
explanation: The ICM is globally recognized for setting the core standards and essential competencies that define basic midwifery training and practice worldwide. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T2#BMP211_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why does the official definition of a midwife specifically emphasize partnership with women?

options.A: To reduce the total number of hospital visits required during the antenatal period
options.B: To respect women's choices and encourage active participation in their own care
options.C: To ensure the midwife takes sole legal blame if a birth complication occurs
options.D: To make sure relatives do not interfere with medical procedures in the labour ward

explanation: Midwifery practice centers around a woman-friendly approach that honors individual autonomy, informed consent, and shared decision-making throughout pregnancy and childbirth. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T2#BMP211_U1_T2_h1)

question: What is a primary duty of a midwife during the postnatal period?

options.A: Assessing uterine involution and checking lochia
options.B: Administering chemotherapy for gestational trophoblastic disease
options.C: Fitting permanent contraceptive implants like tubal ligation
options.D: Performing major abdominal surgery for fibroids

explanation: Checking how the uterus contracts and monitoring lochia are standard postnatal assessments to ensure the mother is recovering safely after childbirth. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T2#BMP211_U1_T2_h2)

question: A midwife notes that a baby born five minutes ago has a slow heart rate and is struggling to breathe. What is the most appropriate immediate action?

options.A: Wait for the attending pediatrician to arrive before touching the infant
options.B: Conduct immediate newborn resuscitation and provide thermal care
options.C: Discharge the mother and baby home immediately to reduce clinic stress
options.D: Prescribe oral antibiotics for suspected neonatal sepsis

explanation: Immediate resuscitation and keeping the newborn warm are core lifesaving responsibilities expected of every trained midwife during intrapartum and neonatal care. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T2#BMP211_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why must a midwife clearly understand the legal limits of their professional scope of practice?

options.A: To guarantee that they receive a higher salary than general nurses
options.B: To prevent practicing outside legal boundaries and ensure patient safety
options.C: To avoid having to document routine clinical procedures in patient files
options.D: To make sure they can perform major surgeries without a doctor present

explanation: Knowing what procedures are permitted prevents malpractice, ensures timely referrals, and protects both the mother and the legal standing of the midwife. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T2#BMP211_U1_T2_h3)

question: Which of the following procedures is NOT within the standard scope of practice for a basic midwife?

options.C: Conducting a normal vertex vaginal delivery

explanation: Major abdominal surgeries like Caesarean sections require specialized medical training as a doctor or obstetrician, falling outside the routine scope of a midwife. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T2#BMP211_U1_T2_h3)

question: What does professional autonomy mean for a practicing midwife?

options.A: Prescribing any medication available in a standard retail pharmacy
options.B: Taking full personal responsibility for clinical decisions during normal childbirth
options.C: Running a private maternity hospital without any government oversight
options.D: Working completely alone without ever needing to consult a doctor

explanation: Autonomy grants the midwife the legal and professional independence to make clinical judgments and manage uncomplicated pregnancies and births on their own authority. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T2#BMP211_U1_T2_h4)

question: Why is collaborative care necessary even though midwives practice autonomously?

options.A: Doctors usually prefer to handle all normal antenatal visits themselves
options.B: Midwives are not permitted by law to touch patients without a doctor's written note
options.C: Complications can develop suddenly, requiring rapid medical intervention and referral
options.D: Collaborative care eliminates the need to document clinical findings in registers

explanation: Because childbirth is dynamic and unpredictable, teamwork and established referral networks ensure high-risk cases receive advanced medical care without delay. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T2#BMP211_U1_T2_h4)

question: Which regulatory body is legally empowered to control and supervise midwifery education and practice in Nigeria?

options.B: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria
options.C: National Association of Nigerian Nurses and Midwives
options.D: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The NMCN is the statutory body charged with regulating education, setting standards, and licensing nursing and midwifery professionals across Nigeria. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T2#BMP211_U1_T2_h5)

question: A midwife continues to practice in a rural clinic despite her professional license having expired two years ago. What regulatory violation has occurred?

options.A: Violating patient confidentiality by discussing case notes publicly
options.B: Overstepping the collaborative referral boundary for normal deliveries
options.C: Failing to obtain informed consent before conducting a vaginal exam
options.D: Practicing illegally without a valid license from the NMCN

explanation: Operating with an expired license violates Nigerian health laws and subjects the practitioner to disciplinary action by the Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria. [learn more](BMP211_U1_T2#BMP211_U1_T2_h5)
